35: // Rewrite is a middleware which can rewrite/mutate HTTP requests.
36: //
37: // The Method and URI properties are "setters" (the request URI

41: // modifiers in a single rewrite.

44: // performed in the URL-decoded (unescaped, normalized) space by
45: // default except for the specific bytes where an escape sequence

49: // multiple, consecutive slashes are collapsed into a single slash,
50: // and dot elements are resolved and removed. In the special case
51: // of a prefix, suffix, or substring containing "//" (repeated slashes),
52: // slashes will not be merged while cleaning the path so that

140: // rewrite performs the rewrites on r using repl, which should
141: // have been obtained from r, but is passed in for efficiency.
142: // It returns true if any changes were made to r.
143: func (rewr Rewrite) Rewrite(r *http.Request, repl *caddy.Replacer) bool {
144: 	oldMethod := r.Method
145: 	oldURI := r.RequestURI
146: 
147: 	// method
148: 	if rewr.Method != "" {
149: 		r.Method = strings.ToUpper(repl.ReplaceAll(rewr.Method, ""))
150: 	}
151: 
152: 	// uri (path, query string and... fragment, because why not)
153: 	if uri := rewr.URI; uri != "" {
154: 		// find the bounds of each part of the URI that exist
155: 		pathStart, qsStart, fragStart := -1, -1, -1
156: 		pathEnd, qsEnd := -1, -1
157: 	loop:
158: 		for i, ch := range uri {
159: 			switch {
160: 			case ch == '?' && qsStart < 0:
161: 				pathEnd, qsStart = i, i+1
162: 			case ch == '#' && fragStart < 0: // everything after fragment is fragment (very clear in RFC 3986 section 4.2)
163: 				if qsStart < 0 {
164: 					pathEnd = i
165: 				} else {
166: 					qsEnd = i
167: 				}
168: 				fragStart = i + 1
169: 				break loop
170: 			case pathStart < 0 && qsStart < 0:
171: 				pathStart = i
172: 			}
173: 		}
174: 		if pathStart >= 0 && pathEnd < 0 {
175: 			pathEnd = len(uri)
176: 		}
177: 		if qsStart >= 0 && qsEnd < 0 {
178: 			qsEnd = len(uri)
179: 		}
180: 
181: 		// isolate the three main components of the URI
182: 		var path, query, frag string
183: 		if pathStart > -1 {
184: 			path = uri[pathStart:pathEnd]
185: 		}
186: 		if qsStart > -1 {
187: 			query = uri[qsStart:qsEnd]
188: 		}
189: 		if fragStart > -1 {
190: 			frag = uri[fragStart:]
191: 		}
192: 
193: 		// build components which are specified, and store them
194: 		// in a temporary variable so that they all read the
195: 		// same version of the URI
196: 		var newPath, newQuery, newFrag string
197: 
198: 		if path != "" {
199: 			// replace the `path` placeholder to escaped path
200: 			pathPlaceholder := "{http.request.uri.path}"
201: 			if strings.Contains(path, pathPlaceholder) {
202: 				path = strings.ReplaceAll(path, pathPlaceholder, r.URL.EscapedPath())
203: 			}
204: 
205: 			newPath = repl.ReplaceAll(path, "")
206: 		}
207: 
208: 		// before continuing, we need to check if a query string
209: 		// snuck into the path component during replacements
210: 		if before, after, found := strings.Cut(newPath, "?"); found {
211: 			// recompute; new path contains a query string
212: 			var injectedQuery string
213: 			newPath, injectedQuery = before, after
214: 			// don't overwrite explicitly-configured query string
215: 			if query == "" {
216: 				query = injectedQuery
217: 			}
218: 		}
219: 
220: 		if query != "" {
221: 			newQuery = buildQueryString(query, repl)
222: 		}
223: 		if frag != "" {
224: 			newFrag = repl.ReplaceAll(frag, "")
225: 		}
226: 
227: 		// update the URI with the new components
228: 		// only after building them
229: 		if pathStart >= 0 {
230: 			if path, err := url.PathUnescape(newPath); err != nil {
231: 				r.URL.Path = newPath
232: 			} else {
233: 				r.URL.Path = path
234: 			}
235: 		}
236: 		if qsStart >= 0 {
237: 			r.URL.RawQuery = newQuery
238: 		}
239: 		if fragStart >= 0 {
240: 			r.URL.Fragment = newFrag
241: 		}
242: 	}
243: 
244: 	// strip path prefix or suffix
245: 	if rewr.StripPathPrefix != "" {
246: 		prefix := repl.ReplaceAll(rewr.StripPathPrefix, "")
247: 		mergeSlashes := !strings.Contains(prefix, "//")
248: 		changePath(r, func(escapedPath string) string {
249: 			escapedPath = caddyhttp.CleanPath(escapedPath, mergeSlashes)
250: 			return trimPathPrefix(escapedPath, prefix)
251: 		})
252: 	}
253: 	if rewr.StripPathSuffix != "" {
254: 		suffix := repl.ReplaceAll(rewr.StripPathSuffix, "")
255: 		mergeSlashes := !strings.Contains(suffix, "//")
256: 		changePath(r, func(escapedPath string) string {
257: 			escapedPath = caddyhttp.CleanPath(escapedPath, mergeSlashes)

259: 		})
260: 	}
261: 
262: 	// substring replacements in URI
263: 	for _, rep := range rewr.URISubstring {
264: 		repl.ApplyURISubstring(rep, r)
265: 	}
266: 
267: 	// regular expression replacements on the path
268: 	for _, rep := range rewr.PathRegexp {
269: 		rep.do(r, repl)
270: 	}
271: 
272: 	// update the encoded copy of the URI
273: 	r.RequestURI = r.URL.RequestURI()

275: 	// return true if anything changed
276: 	return r.Method != oldMethod || r.RequestURI != oldURI

279: // buildQueryString takes an input query string and
280: // performs replacements on each component, returning
281: // the resulting query string. This function appends
282: // duplicate keys rather than replaces.
283: func buildQueryString(qs string, repl *caddy.Replacer) string {
284: 	var sb strings.Builder
285: 
286: 	// first component must be key, which is the same
287: 	// as if we just wrote a value in previous iteration
288: 	wroteVal := true
289: 
290: 	for len(qs) > 0 {
291: 		// determine the end of this component, which will be at
292: 		// the next equal sign or ampersand, whichever comes first
293: 		nextEq, nextAmp := strings.Index(qs, "="), strings.Index(qs, "&")
294: 		ampIsNext := nextAmp >= 0 && (nextAmp < nextEq || nextEq < 0)
295: 		end := len(qs) // assume no delimiter remains...
296: 		if ampIsNext {
297: 			end = nextAmp // ...unless ampersand is first...
298: 		} else if nextEq >= 0 && (nextEq < nextAmp || nextAmp < 0) {
299: 			end = nextEq // ...or unless equal is first.
300: 		}
301: 
302: 		// consume the component and write the result
303: 		comp := qs[:end]
304: 		comp, _ = repl.ReplaceFunc(comp, func(name string, val any) (any, error) {
305: 			if name == "http.request.uri.query" && wroteVal {
306: 				return val, nil // already escaped
307: 			}
308: 			var valStr string
309: 			switch v := val.(type) {
310: 			case string:
311: 				valStr = v
312: 			case fmt.Stringer:
313: 				valStr = v.String()
314: 			case int:
315: 				valStr = strconv.Itoa(v)
316: 			default:
317: 				valStr = fmt.Sprintf("%+v", v)
318: 			}
319: 			return url.QueryEscape(valStr), nil
320: 		})
321: 		if end < len(qs) {
322: 			end++ // consume delimiter
323: 		}
324: 		qs = qs[end:]
325: 
326: 		// if previous iteration wrote a value,
327: 		// that means we are writing a key
328: 		if wroteVal {
329: 			if sb.Len() > 0 && len(comp) > 0 {
330: 				sb.WriteRune('&')
331: 			}
332: 		} else {
333: 			sb.WriteRune('=')
334: 		}
335: 		sb.WriteString(comp)
336: 
337: 		// remember for the next iteration that we just wrote a value,
338: 		// which means the next iteration MUST write a key
339: 		wroteVal = ampIsNext
340: 	}
341: 
342: 	return sb.String()
343: }

345: // trimPathPrefix is like strings.TrimPrefix, but customized for advanced URI
346: // path prefix matching. The string prefix will be trimmed from the beginning
347: // of escapedPath if escapedPath starts with prefix. Rather than a naive 1:1
348: // comparison of each byte to determine if escapedPath starts with prefix,
349: // both strings are iterated in lock-step, and if prefix has a '%' encoding
350: // at a particular position, escapedPath must also have the same encoding
351: // representation for that character. In other words, if the prefix string
352: // uses the escaped form for a character, escapedPath must literally use the
353: // same escape at that position. Otherwise, all character comparisons are
354: // performed in normalized/unescaped space.
355: func trimPathPrefix(escapedPath, prefix string) string {
356: 	var iPath, iPrefix int
357: 	for {
358: 		if iPath >= len(escapedPath) || iPrefix >= len(prefix) {
359: 			break
360: 		}
361: 
362: 		prefixCh := prefix[iPrefix]
363: 		ch := string(escapedPath[iPath])
364: 
365: 		if ch == "%" && prefixCh != '%' && len(escapedPath) >= iPath+3 {
366: 			var err error
367: 			ch, err = url.PathUnescape(escapedPath[iPath : iPath+3])
368: 			if err != nil {
369: 				// should be impossible unless EscapedPath() is returning invalid values!
370: 				return escapedPath
371: 			}
372: 			iPath += 2
373: 		}
374: 
375: 		// prefix comparisons are case-insensitive to consistency with
376: 		// path matcher, which is case-insensitive for good reasons
377: 		if !strings.EqualFold(ch, string(prefixCh)) {
378: 			return escapedPath
379: 		}
380: 
381: 		iPath++
382: 		iPrefix++
383: 	}
384: 
385: 	// if we iterated through the entire prefix, we found it, so trim it
386: 	if iPath >= len(prefix) {
387: 		return escapedPath[iPath:]
388: 	}
389: 
390: 	// otherwise we did not find the prefix
391: 	return escapedPath
392: }

394: func reverse(s string) string {
395: 	r := []rune(s)
396: 	for i, j := 0, len(r)-1; i < len(r)/2; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
397: 		r[i], r[j] = r[j], r[i]
398: 	}
399: 	return string(r)
400: }

403: type substrReplacer = caddy.URISubstring

405: // regexReplacer describes a replacement using a regular expression.
406: type regexReplacer struct {
407: 	// The regular expression to find.
408: 	Find string `json:"find,omitempty"`
409: 
410: 	// The substring to replace with. Supports placeholders and
411: 	// regular expression capture groups.
412: 	Replace string `json:"replace,omitempty"`

414: 	re *regexp.Regexp
415: }

417: func (rep regexReplacer) do(r *http.Request, repl *caddy.Replacer) {
418: 	if rep.Find == "" || rep.re == nil {
419: 		return
420: 	}
421: 	replace := repl.ReplaceAll(rep.Replace, "")
422: 	changePath(r, func(pathOrRawPath string) string {
423: 		return rep.re.ReplaceAllString(pathOrRawPath, replace)
424: 	})

427: func changePath(req *http.Request, newVal func(pathOrRawPath string) string) {
428: 	req.URL.RawPath = newVal(req.URL.EscapedPath())
429: 	if p, err := url.PathUnescape(req.URL.RawPath); err == nil && p != "" {
430: 		req.URL.Path = p
431: 	} else {
432: 		req.URL.Path = newVal(req.URL.Path)
433: 	}
434: 	// RawPath is only set if it's different from the normalized Path (std lib)
435: 	if req.URL.RawPath == req.URL.Path {
436: 		req.URL.RawPath = ""
437: 	}
438: }

298: // and processes the text to strip leading whitespace, returning the final

301: 	stringVal := string(val)
302: 
303: 	// find the last newline of the heredoc, which is where the contents end
304: 	lastNewline := strings.LastIndex(stringVal, "\n")
305: 
306: 	// collapse the content, then split into separate lines

144: // block will be consumed internally and omitted from

179: 		d.cursor-- // roll back if not opening brace
180: 		return false
181: 	}

183: 	if d.Val() == "}" {
184: 		return false // open and then closed right away

262: // Args is a convenience function that loads the next arguments
263: // (tokens on the same line) into an arbitrary number of strings
264: // pointed to in targets. If there are not enough argument tokens

266: // targets are left unchanged. If all the targets are filled,

269: 	for i := 0; i < len(targets); i++ {
270: 		if !d.NextArg() {
271: 			return false
272: 		}
273: 		*targets[i] = d.Val()

280: // number of available argument tokens must match the number of
281: // targets exactly to return true.

284: 		return false

296: 	count := 0
297: 	for d.NextArg() {
298: 		count++
299: 	}
300: 	for i := 0; i < count; i++ {

307: // into a slice and returns them. Open curly brace tokens also indicate

309: // the return value nor is it loaded.

311: 	var args []string
312: 	for d.NextArg() {
313: 		args = append(args, d.Val())
314: 	}

319: // retaining quotes) into a slice and returns them. Open curly brace
320: // tokens also indicate the end of arguments, and the curly brace is
321: // not included in the return value nor is it loaded.

323: 	var args []string
324: 	for d.NextArg() {
325: 		args = append(args, d.ValRaw())

330: // NewFromNextSegment returns a new dispenser with a copy of
331: // the tokens from the current token until the end of the
332: // "directive" whether that be to the end of the line or

339: // NextSegment returns a copy of the tokens from the current
340: // token until the end of the line or block that starts at
341: // the end of the line.
342: func (d *Dispenser) NextSegment() Segment {
343: 	tkns := Segment{d.Token()}

345: 		tkns = append(tkns, d.Token())

348: 	for nesting := d.Nesting(); d.NextBlock(nesting); {

351: 			// curly brace, we rewind here to append it, since

355: 			d.Prev()
356: 			tkns = append(tkns, d.Token())

358: 			openedBlock = true
359: 		}
360: 		tkns = append(tkns, d.Token())
361: 	}
362: 	if openedBlock {
363: 		// include closing brace
364: 		tkns = append(tkns, d.Token())

366: 		// do not consume the closing curly brace; the
367: 		// next iteration of the enclosing loop will
368: 		// call Next() and consume it
